## TL;DR

RepoOS Hub’s Capacitor shell (`mobile/`) now matches the web app’s themes and feels native on iOS and Android: a dedicated Settings page (appearance, device lock, about), redesigned server list with edit-mode reorder and bottom-sheet edit/delete, Lucide icons, platform-specific styling, and theme/mode persistence. Browser dev fixtures and a `repoos-mobile-dev` preview target support review screenshots at phone size. Automated tests cover theme persistence and fixtures; on-device flash-free boot and store installs remain human follow-ups.

## Work and rationale

The prior shell inlined device lock above the server list, used text-arrow reorder controls, and shipped a single dark palette. The task asked for parity with `src/ui-app` themes plus light/dark/system, Lucide icons, and preferences moved off the picker screen.

Theme wiring reuses `mobile/src/design-tokens` and a generated `ui-themes.css` (via `mobile/scripts/sync-ui-theme-vars.mjs`) so every web design theme works in light and dark. `theme-core.ts` holds pure logic tested from `src/ui-app/tests/mobile-hub-shell.test.ts`; Capacitor Preferences persistence stays in `theme.ts`. An inline boot script in `mobile/index.html` reads the same preference keys (and optional `?theme=` / `?appearance=` query params for shots) before Vue mounts to avoid a first-paint flash in the browser dev harness; native Capacitor applies prefs in `app-state.init()`.

Navigation is route-based inside `App.vue`: picker (default), settings, add server, plus a `BottomSheet` for edit/delete. Device lock UI lives only under Settings. `ServerListView` provides avatar tiles, reachability indicators, empty state, edit-mode drag reorder with haptics on delete, and platform classes from `platform.ts` (`?platform=ios|android` for shots). Android gets ripple/elevation patterns; iOS gets grouped list styling in `style.css`.

Icons come from `lucide-vue-next` (the only new runtime dependency in `mobile/package.json`). Existing HTTPS-only add flow, reachability checks, Preferences-backed server list, InAppBrowser open, and lock screen behaviour are unchanged.

For review evidence, `mobile/src/fixture.ts` seeds list states via `?fixture=empty|one|many|unreachable|settings|add`. Declared `## Shots` use 390×844 viewports with `?platform=` / `?theme=` / `?appearance=` overrides. **Sign-off blocker:** add a `[[preview.targets]]` row named `repoos-mobile-dev` (`areas = ["mobile"]`, `paths = ["mobile/**"]`, `cwd = "mobile"`, `command = "bun run dev -- --port {port} --host {host} --strictPort"`, `readyPath = "/"`) then re-declare shots with `"target": "repoos-mobile-dev"` so capture does not boot the main RepoOS server. `src/core/shot-page.ts` now screenshots the first match when a selector resolves to multiple elements (fixing `#app` duplication after removing duplicate id from `src/ui-app/src/App.vue`).

## Approaches tried

- **Pinia vs module state:** Kept the existing small `app-state.ts` ref module; a store would add ceremony for four screens.
- **Theme source of truth:** Synced CSS variables from the web app rather than hand-copying palettes, so new web themes only need the sync script re-run.
- **Reorder UX:** Edit-mode with drag handles instead of always-visible arrow buttons — clearer on touch and closer to platform list-edit patterns.
- **Preview routing:** Path glob `mobile/**` plus `area: mobile` so mixed diffs still resolve the hub target when appropriate.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Shot target gap:** Repo had no preview row for the mobile Vite app; shots naming `repoos-mobile-dev` failed validation until the `[[preview.targets]]` entry landed.
- **On-device criteria:** Task `needs_input` correctly flags Capacitor Preferences flash-free behaviour and physical device polish; this pass proves browser-target screenshots and unit tests only.
- **`just build-android`:** Not re-run in this session; acceptance criterion 8 treats a successful Android build as conditional on local SDK tooling.

## Key learnings

- The hub shell should stay a thin picker: no RepoOS board routes in Capacitor — fixtures are query-param driven on the dev server only.
- Platform styling via `document.documentElement.platform-*` and shot overrides is cheaper than separate builds while still showing Android vs iOS chrome in review PNGs.
- Declaring a preview target is part of shipping mobile UI in this repo: without `paths = ["mobile/**"]`, handoff capture would fall through to the main app preview and mislead reviewers.

## Human follow-ups (not claimed done)

1. Install debug APK / iOS build on hardware and confirm theme persistence and status-bar theming with no flash.
2. Run `just build-android` when Android toolchain is available.
3. Optional: split a human-only task for on-device verification if close-out should not wait on Nick’s phone.
